name: Schedule the admission test and assign the teacher who will conduct it
priorityReason: Without it the office works out free slots and free teachers by hand, which is where admissions stall.

goal.capability: to set the test date and time and assign a free teacher in one step
goal.outcome: the family and the teacher are both told, and nobody has to check a timetable by hand

secondaryActors.involvement: Receives the date and time on the number given on the form.
Is assigned to conduct the test, receives the schedule, and conducts it on the day.
Handles requests to change the slot.

additional.description: An admission form is submitted and the applicant enters the scheduling queue.

A reminder goes to the family and the assigned teacher the day before the test.

preconditions.condition: An applicant exists at status Form submitted, carrying a temporary ID.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin.
The school's working hours are configured, so a slot can be recommended.

establishedBy.name: Class, section and academic session structure

preconditions.condition: Timetable and staff attendance data exist, so teacher availability can be determined.

postConditions: The applicant carries a test date, time and an assigned teacher, all saved against the temporary ID.
The slot is booked, so it is not recommended to another applicant.
The family has been sent the date and time on the number given on the form, and the send is logged with its delivery status.
The assigned teacher has the schedule and the applicant appears in their list for the day.
The applicant is ready for marking; no score exists yet.
Where the schedule or the teacher is later changed, both the family and the teacher concerned are told again, and the previous assignment stays in the history.

businessRules.rule: The test is scheduled against the applicant's temporary ID. Everything from here to the decision hangs off that identifier.
The system recommends a slot from the school's working hours and the slots already booked. The recommendation is a default, and the admin may enter a slot of their own.
Only teachers free at the selected slot are listed, drawn from the timetable and staff attendance. Changing the slot re-computes the list, because a teacher free at nine may be teaching at eleven.
The admin may enter a teacher directly where none of the free ones is suitable. The override is recorded with a reason, because it may put the teacher in two places at once.
A directly entered teacher is checked against their timetable and the clash is shown. It is not blocked, because the school may have a reason; it is shown so the choice is deliberate.
Saving the schedule sends the date and time to the contact number on the form and to the assigned teacher, and logs both sends with their delivery status.
A rescheduled test, or a change of teacher, resends the details to the family and to the teacher concerned, and requires a reason. The previous assignment stays in the history.
Where a teacher is replaced, the teacher removed is told as well, so nobody turns up for a test that is no longer theirs.
The admin may send the schedule to the parents of all approved applicants at once rather than one at a time. Each send is logged individually, and a failure for one does not stop the rest.
A booked slot is not recommended to another applicant, so the recommendation does not create a double booking.
Scheduling records no score and takes no decision. It sets a time and a person.

transitions.condition: A date, time and teacher are saved and both parties are notified (BR-6).
The slot or the teacher changes, with a reason (BR-7).
The applicant attends and the test is conducted (UC-02-06).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicants awaiting a test
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the completed admission form from the pending list.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the applicant, their approved class and their submitted form.
Recommends a date and time from the school's working hours and the slots already booked.

basicFlow.navigation: Schedule admission test → Date and time
basicFlow.userAction: Accepts the recommendation, or enters a date and time of their own.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates the slot is within working hours and is not already booked.
Lists only the teachers free at that slot, drawn from the timetable and staff attendance. Changing the slot re-computes the list.

basicFlow.userAction: Selects one of the free teachers, or enters a teacher directly with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the assignment, and where a teacher was entered directly, shows any timetable clash and records the override.

basicFlow.navigation: Schedule admission test → Save and notify
basicFlow.systemResponse: Saves the date, time, venue and teacher against the temporary ID and books the slot.
Sends the date and time to the contact number on the form and to the assigned teacher, and logs both sends with their delivery status.

alternateFlows.condition: None of the free teachers is suitable
alternateFlows.navigation: Schedule admission test → Enter a teacher directly
alternateFlows.behaviour: The admin names a teacher outside the free list and gives a reason. Any timetable clash is shown but not blocked, so the choice is deliberate rather than accidental (BR-4, BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: Several approved applicants are being scheduled at once
alternateFlows.navigation: Applicants awaiting a test → Schedule in bulk
alternateFlows.behaviour: The admin schedules a group and the details are sent to every parent and every assigned teacher. Each send is logged individually and one failure does not stop the rest (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The family asks for a different date
alternateFlows.behaviour: The slot is changed with a reason. The family and the assigned teacher are told again, and the previous slot stays in the history (BR-7).
A replacement is assigned with a reason. Both the new teacher and the one removed are told, so nobody turns up for a test that is no longer theirs (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The applicant is a re-admission with no admission form
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Re-admission applicants → Schedule test
alternateFlows.behaviour: The applicant reaches scheduling from the re-admission path rather than from a completed form. Everything else is the same.

departures.requirement: The free-teacher list for a slot returns within 2 seconds across a staff of 200, since it is recomputed every time the slot changes.

A schedule is never reported as sent until the provider accepts it. A failed message leaves the schedule intact and visibly unsent.

openQuestions.question: Should a directly entered teacher with a timetable clash be blocked rather than warned?
openQuestions.assumption: Warned, not blocked. The school may have a reason (BR-5).

openQuestions.question: How long is an admission test slot, and can two applicants share one?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. It decides whether the recommendation books a slot or a seat.

openQuestions.question: Does the assigned teacher have to be a subject specialist for the approved class?
openQuestions.assumption: No. Any free teacher may be assigned.

openQuestions.question: Who conducts the test if the assigned teacher is absent on the day?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. There is no automatic reassignment.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
